questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Dr. Ritu was explain the (1)/ benefits of doing yoga at (2)/ least four times a week. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The error lies in part 1 of the sentence as the verb ‘explain’ does not fit with the verb ‘was’. The sentence talks about a regular activity thus the correct tense here is simple present. It should read as:’Dr.Ritu explains the.’

questions.solution: The error lies in part 2 as the verb ‘is’ should be replaced with ‘are’. The subject must agree with the verb. The subject here is plural,’problems’, thus the verb should be ‘are.’ It should read as:’socio-economic problems are still.’

**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Unless you do not (1)/ give up bad habits (2)/ you will suffer. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: The word ‘unless’ and ‘do not’ cannot be placed together. ‘Unless’ means ‘except if (used to introduce the case in which a statement being made is not true or valid).’ Either the words ‘do not’ should be eliminated or ‘unless’ should be replaced with ‘if’. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

It was very hot, you _________ your jackets.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e. **'Need not have brought'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sentence describes **an action in the past that, in hindsight, was not necessary. Therefore, the correct phrase needs to express a past unnecessary action.
 
• **"Need not have brought"** (Option 2) correctly conveys that bringing the jackets was not necessary and is used for actions that were done but, in hindsight, were not needed.
 
• The structure** "need not have + past participle" **is used to talk about actions that were completed in the past but were unnecessary.
 
• The sentence is set in the past, indicating that the decision to bring the jackets was made before realizing it was very hot. "Need not have brought" captures this sense of past unnecessary action.
 
• This option correctly follows the rules of modal verbs in English grammar, particularly **"need not,"** which is followed by "have" and a past participle when talking about unnecessary past actions.

Therefore, the** correct answer** is- **'Option 2'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "Need not bring,"** is incorrect because it suggests an advice or possibility not to bring the jackets in the future or generally, not addressing the past action.
 
• **Option 3, "Need not brought," **is grammatically incorrect because "need not" should be followed by "have" and a past participle when referring to unnecessary actions in the past.
 
• **Option 4, "Need not had been brought,**" is overly complex and incorrect. The phrase confuses the grammar by incorrectly trying to use a past perfect form with "need not," which is not how unnecessary past actions are typically expressed in English.

• The incorrect spelling is "Skelful". Its correct spelling is "Skillful" which means talented.
 
• Let us look at the meanings of other words:
 
• Fulfil=> achieve or realize (something desired, promised, or predicted)
 
• Willful=> intentional
 
• Shameful=> worthy of or causing shame or disgrace
 
• Thus option 3 is the wrongly spelt word.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Select the incorrectly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Sergeant=> a rank of non-commissioned officer in the army or air force, above corporal and below staff sergeant

Pedestal=> the base or support on which a statue, obelisk, or column is mounted

Scavenger=> an animal that feeds on carrion, dead plant material, or refuse.

Luminescent=> (of a substance) producing light without being heated

Thus option 1 is the wrongly spelt word.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Select the incorrectly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct words are:

Mellifluence=> the quality of sounding very smooth or pleasant

Centenarian=> someone who is a 100 years old or more

Plebiscite=> the direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question such as a change in the constitution.

Analysable=> that which can be analysed

Thus option 3 is the wrongly spelt word.

questions.question: A _________ is made, not born.
questions.solution: The word here should be such that is created or comes into existence with time and not born. ‘Nuance’ which means ‘a subtle difference in or shade of meaning, expression, or sound; does not fit here. The word ‘coinage’ means ‘coins collectively or the invention of a new word or phrase.’ The word ‘cliché’ means ‘a phrase or opinion that is overused and betrays a lack of original thought’ and fits here conveying the meaning that it is made or deliberately used and not comes on its own. The word ‘current’ means ‘ongoing’ and makes no sense here. Thus option 3 is the correct answer

questions.question: new way of stating a _________ experience.
questions.solution: The word ‘common’ which means ‘general or ordinary’ fits as the correct adjective here. The other words make no sense here. ‘Authentic’ means ‘of undisputed origin and not a copy; genuine’ and ‘mental’ means ‘relating to the mind’. The word ‘rational’ means ‘logical’ and it does not make any sense that the process of a cliché starts with a logical experience. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: the remark is an _________.
questions.solution:
The meanings of the words are:

Epigram=> a short saying or poem that expresses an idea in a clever, funny way

Epitaph=> a phrase or form of words written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone

Epilogue=> a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened

Epicenter=> the point on the earth's surface vertically above the focus of an earthquake

Thus option 1 is the correct answer as it states what the remark should be like.

questions.question: it is particularly _________ as well as catchy
questions.solution: The saying receives a wide circulation thus the word ‘vague’ which means ‘unclear’ cannot fit here. The word ‘apt’ means ‘appropriate’ and justifies how the saying receives circulation. The word ‘ingenuine’ means ‘unreal’ and ‘emotional’ which means ‘relating to a person's emotions‘ do not fit here.

questions.question: likely to be _________ from overwork.
questions.solution: The word ‘overwork’ makes it clear that the word here should have a negative meaning. Thus ‘suffering’ is the correct word. ‘Overlooked’ means ‘failed to notice’ and is incorrect here. The word ‘inducing’ means ‘bring about or give rise to’ and does not fit here. Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: According to the passage, which among the following is the major contributor to India's GDP growth?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘The rural economy is an important segment of the ecosystem and accounts for around 70 percent of employment and 50 percent of GDP with **agriculture** being the **main driver** followed by services and manufacturing.’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What has become a haven for routing black money in India?

options.text: Cash transactions over digital cash transactions

questions.solution: Black money can be routed only when there is no proper record thus options 2,3 and 4 are eliminated. It is mentioned in the passage that technology is not much used in the transactions and cash is mostly used which creates a shelter for routing black money. Thus option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a kharif crop?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘*This has happened just when we are in middle of the kharif harvest which involves rice, soybean, cotton, maize, sugarcane, bajra, besides fruits and vegetables which are all year through.’ *Wheat is not mentioned here thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Why does demonetisation has lesser impact onto the rabi season?
questions.solution: It is mentioned in the passage ‘*The issue here is less serious as a large part is backed by credit where the prevalent cash crunch may not matter*.’ Due to support from the credit payments demonetization would have lesser impact on the rabi season. Thus option 3 is the correct answer

questions.question: Which of the following is not true in regards to rural economy?

options.text: It account for major percent in employmenting the people of the country.
It has a technology driven mandis.
Major transactions are based on cash.
Demonetization has caused significant distortions in rural economy especially to farmers.

questions.solution: The passage clearly states that rural economy lacks technology and the mandis run on cash. It is mentioned in the passage ‘*Almost all transactions in the mandis (there are above 7,000 organized ones and over double the number that is unorganized), are based on cash as it is easy to use.*’ Thus option 2 is the correct answer.
